assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a scalar boson at the LHC completed the experimental basis of the electroweak sector and is a discovery of the first rank; it is the kind of finding I would put at the centre. The prize for the theory has already been given, so the natural complement is the experimental achievement itself, conceived and built as two large detectors that confirmed each other independently.
assessment.attribution: The ATLAS and CMS collaborations comprise thousands of people, so any trio is a simplification. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are credited as the conceivers and long-term leaders of the detector projects, which is a defensible reading of who stood behind the discovery; the physics-analysis leadership in 2012 is a different group and the committee would have to argue the principle.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: discovery announced in 2012, couplings and spin-parity measured over more than a decade, and two independent experiments agree. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee is willing to honour detector conception and construction rather than the 2012 analysis leaders, and whether three names can represent two collaborations fairly.
I have not verified the exact formal roles of each credited person; this rests on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's precision maps of the microwave background fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level and turned cosmology into a quantitative science; the acoustic peaks, the flat geometry and the age of the universe followed. This is a major and lasting measurement, though COBE and the earlier prize for dark energy partly cover the surrounding territory.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as principal investigator, Page was central to the instrument and calibration, and Spergel to the cosmological interpretation. This is a reasonable trio, though other WMAP team members and the late David Wilkinson could be argued for; Wilkinson is not eligible.
assessment.maturity: Mature: results from 2003 onward, confirmed independently by Planck and ground-based experiments, with a stable interpretation as LCDM.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 prize for CMB anisotropy and the 2011 prize for accelerating expansion may lead some to judge the marginal novelty smaller.
Exact division of credit within the WMAP science team is not settled by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos and their association with a flaring blazar and later with the Galactic plane opened a genuinely new window on the high-energy universe. A cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice was a bold concept that delivered a clear discovery, in the line of earlier neutrino-astronomy recognition.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the conceiver and long-term scientific leader of IceCube, and the only name supplied. A single laureate is a clean configuration, but the collaboration is large and AMANDA predecessors and other leaders contributed; I cannot judge from the supplied text whether one person captures the decisive role.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the 2013 discovery has been confirmed by multiple analyses, with source associations in 2018 and 2023 and corroboration from other telescopes, though the identification of the sources is still incomplete.
uncertainties: Whether a single-person prize is fair given the scale of the collaboration.
Source identification is still developing, so the astrophysical interpretation is not finished.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall state introduced a new classification of matter and a robust edge-transport phenomenon, with wide influence. It is conceptually clean and experimentally confirmed, and has an obvious link to topological ideas already recognised by the committee.
assessment.attribution: Kane contributed the decisive time-reversal-invariant theory with Mele, and Molenkamp's group made the first observation in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied credit list omits Mele, Zhang (deceased), Bernevig and Hasan, so any trio excludes someone with a strong claim; I keep Xue out because his quantum anomalous Hall result is a distinct sub-discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of confirmation in many materials, with a stable interpretation.
uncertainties: Genuinely contested priority among several theorists and the separate three-dimensional case, which complicates a fair trio.
The candidate bundles quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall results that may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of afterglows ended the long debate over the distance scale of gamma-ray bursts and established their cosmological origin, with a huge energy release that led to the study of the most luminous explosions. This is a discovery in the plain sense, with clear lasting effect.
assessment.attribution: The X-ray afterglow came from the BeppoSAX team (Costa, Frontera) and the optical and redshift confirmations from several groups; Kulkarni's group was prominent in the redshift and the theory of the burst environment. Van Paradijs, who made the optical detection, is deceased, which weakens a full account of credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: 1997 findings, followed by an enormous body of afterglow and host-galaxy work and later links to supernovae and gravitational-wave events.
uncertainties: The allocation among the BeppoSAX, optical and radio groups is not resolved by the supplied credit, and a deceased key contributor cannot be included.
Time since the discovery means timeliness is a point against, though not decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of a trapped-ion quantum computer and its experimental realisation, including entangling gates and digital quantum simulation, forms a coherent theory-and-experiment story and the leading platform for controlled quantum systems. Part of the experimental toolbox was already honoured in 2012, which narrows the remaining gap.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal, and Blatt's group demonstrated many of the key operations; Wineland is already a laureate. The trio is a fairly clean one, though the credit overlaps with the optical-lattice and Rydberg candidates for Zoller and Cirac.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with two decades of experiments, but scalability of useful computation is still open and some may judge the stage premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2012 prize and with other candidates that share the same theorists.
Whether recognition should wait for a demonstrated advantage in computation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the later discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the whole field of moire quantum materials. This is an original and rapidly influential discovery with clear experimental support.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental observation. The supplied credit supports a two- or three-person prize; I propose the decisive theorist and experimentalist, and note that Bistritzer's claim is real.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature given its age of under a decade, with many groups reproducing the effect, though the origin of the superconductivity is not settled and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Premature relative to older candidates; mechanism of superconductivity remains debated.
Choice between Bistritzer and MacDonald for the theory credit is not resolved by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance underpin the idea that large quantum computers are possible in principle, and the topological codes have shaped both theory and hardware. The concepts are original and important, and recent below-threshold experiments give some physical confirmation.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane gave the first codes, and Kitaev the toric code and fault-tolerance via anyons; Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill and others also contributed, so the trio omits claims. This is a weaker fit for a physics discovery than for a computer-science style invention.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are old but experimental validation is recent and the practical consequence is still unfolding, so recognition may be somewhat early for the hardware outcome.
uncertainties: Several equally strong contributors outside the credited list.
The experimental demonstrations are recent and the long-term outcome is not settled.
